title: Cap. IV Arg. 8 Sol: Remonstrant syllogism on foresight-robes is mere trifles; apply to elect
pass_a_gloss: Let the syllogism therefore be made after the pattern proposed by the Remonstrants, and its vanity will at once be plain: He and such as this King crowned in time, him and such he decreed from the beginning to crown: But he crowns in time one beautifully clothed and purged from his squalor, as such: Therefore from the beginning he decreed to adopt and crown one beautifully clothed, as such, that is, from the foresight condition of beautiful garments. Mere trifles. For the first will of adopting and crowning did not take its origin from an antecedent consideration, or from the foresight condition of beautiful garments; but the very act of crowning required these garments and this antecedent purging, and that from the King's decree ordering the external execution of the thing. Let us accommodate these things to the present design. God wills to adopt Peter, Paul, or any elect corrupted in the mass of old Adam and wasting with sin, from the mere good pleasure of his will, and to gift eternal life: But he also decrees, and promulgates this decree in the Gospel, that he wills that he first be purified by faith, and cleansed from the filth of sins, before he is introduced into possession of the kingdom.
pass_b_english: Run the Remonstrants' pattern and its vanity shows at once: whom and as such this king crowned in time, he decreed from the start to crown as such; but in time he crowns one beautifully clothed and purged of squalor as such; therefore from the start he decreed to adopt and crown one beautifully clothed as such — i.e. from foresight of fair garments. Mere trifles. The first will to adopt and crown did not spring from foresight of garments; crowning itself required those garments and that prior purging, by the king's decree ordering external execution. Apply it: God from mere good pleasure wills to adopt Peter, Paul, or any elect corrupt in old Adam's mass and wasting in sin, and gift eternal life — yet also decrees, and publishes in the Gospel, that he wills him first purified by faith and cleansed from sin's filth before entering the kingdom.
source_text: Fiat ergo syllogismus ad exemplar propositum a Remonstrantibus, et vanitas ejus illico patebit: Ille et talis quem et qualem hic Rex in tempore coronavit, illum et talem ab initio coronare decrevit: Sed pulchre vestitum et a squalore suo purgatum, qua talem, in tempore coronat: Ergo ab initio decrevit pulchre vestitum, qua talem, hoc est, ex praevisa conditione pulchrorum vestimentorum, adoptare et coronare. Nugae merae. Non enim prima voluntas adoptandi et coronandi originem cepit ab antecedanea consideratione, aut praevisa conditione pulchrorum vestimentorum; sed ipsa actio coronandi requirebat haec vestimenta et hanc purgationem antecedaneam, idque ex decreto Regis externam rei exsecutionem ordinante. Accommodemus haec praesenti instituto. Deus Petrum, Paulum, vel quemlibet electum in massa veteris Adami corruptum et peccato tabidum, ex beneplacito mero voluntatis suae vult adoptare, et aeterna vita donare: Sed decernit etiam, et in Evangelio hoc decretum promulgat, velle se ut fide prius purificetur, et a sordibus peccatorum mundetur, quam in possessionem regni introducatur.
